children: Denmark’s seasonally adjusted trade surplus widened to DKK 40.5 billion in July 2026, from a downwardly revised DKK 25.3 billion in June, marking the largest surplus in the current series.
Total exports rose 4.0% month-on-month to DKK 202.7 billion, with goods exports increasing 4.5% to DKK 118.9 billion and services exports rising 3.3% to DKK 83.8 billion.
Meanwhile, imports fell 4.4% to DKK 162.2 billion, driven by a 6.9% decline in goods imports, while services imports decreased 1.4%.

In the first seven months of 2026, total exports reached DKK 1,313.0 billion, up from DKK 1,236.5 billion a year earlier, while imports rose to DKK 1,113.2 billion from DKK 1,045.8 billion with Denmark recorded a trade surplus of DKK 199.8 billion, up from DKK 190.7 billion in the same period of 2025.

title: Denmark Trade Surplus Widens in July
